A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same LESA research work. All 14 pages of each version, including supplementary Sections 6–7, equations, figures, and tables, are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original image- and video-generation experiments, acceleration measurements, component ablations, training-prompt sensitivity, and memory comparisons in Tables 1–9.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results, including the main generation experiments and supplementary evaluations of distilled models and Stable Diffusion XL.

M1.justification: The linear feature projection, KAN scalar modulation, stage-specific predictors, residual update, and two-stage training remain unchanged. New Section 6.3 discusses the existing predictor rather than changing its procedure.

E1.justification: Both retain the same training prompts, DrawBench image evaluations, and HunyuanVideo video evaluations. FLUX variants, Qwen-Image variants, and Stable Diffusion XL were already evaluated in v1; no task or test scenario is added.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged within the corresponding main and supplementary experiments, including TaylorSeer, FORA, ToCa, DuCa, and the Stable Diffusion XL comparison with DeepCache. The newly cited work is not an evaluated baseline.

E3.justification: Sections 7.1–7.2 retain the evaluation metrics, resolutions, 200 DrawBench prompts, 956 video prompts, hardware assignments, and training settings, including one ground-truth-guided epoch followed by two autoregressive epochs.

E4.justification: The interval, segmentation, and KAN-versus-MLP ablations in Table 4, memory analysis in Table 8, prompt-count study in Table 9, and qualitative cases are unchanged. Section 6.3 adds mathematical reasoning, not another empirical analysis.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-seed estimates, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The statement about using 956 prompts, with one video per prompt, to reduce sample-wise variance is unchanged.

E6.justification: Tables 1–9 retain their result entries, and the figures retain their qualitative findings. For example, Qwen-Image LESA at N=7 remains at PSNR 30.18, SSIM 0.78, and LPIPS 0.25; HunyuanVideo at N=7 retains PSNR 21.43.

T1.justification: New supplementary Section 6.3 introduces a second-order finite-difference formulation and an algebraic decomposition into Taylor-like main terms and cross terms in Equations 16–17. Existing method equations and the KAN–MLP derivation are retained.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same stage-aware KAN predictor, two-stage training, and acceleration-versus-quality claims. The appendix addition does not redefine the central contributions.

C2.justification: Section 6.3 newly argues that scalar modulation covers Taylor expansion's main terms while introducing learnable cross terms, providing a broader learning space. This adds a mechanism interpretation; existing empirical interpretations and applicability statements remain unchanged.

D1.justification: The abstract replaces the statement that code accompanies supplementary materials and will be released with an explicit LESA GitHub repository link. Implementation details, hyperparameters, precision, and hardware disclosures remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v3 adds Huang et al., 'Diffusion dataset condensation: Training your diffusion model faster with less data,' to Section 2.2 and the references. Section 6.3 also expands the existing conceptual comparison with TaylorSeer without broadly repositioning the work.

P1.justification: v3 adds the short Scalar Modulation subsection, equal-contribution and corresponding-author notes, and a funding acknowledgment. The remaining narrative and section organization are largely retained, with only small wording and punctuation edits.

P2.justification: Figures 1–7 and Tables 1–9 retain their content and designs. Author footnotes and the added appendix subsection produce local spacing, column, and page reflow, including movement of the supplementary ablation discussion.

improvement.justification: v3 modestly improves documentation by providing a concrete code location and making the intended scalar-modulation rationale explicit in Section 6.3. The new algebra is schematic and does not itself establish the claimed broader learning space, so its theoretical benefit is limited. The method and empirical evidence remain unchanged.
